intended_object: The list of darts (oriented edges) that a walk u = v₀, v₁, …, vₙ = v traverses, in order: [(v₀,v₁), (v₁,v₂), …, (vₙ₋₁,vₙ)]. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition works by recursion on the walk:
- The empty walk `nil` has no darts, so it gives the empty list.
- For a walk `cons h p`, where `h : G.Adj u x` and `p : G.Walk x v`, it puts the dart `(u, x)` (with adjacency proof `h`) in front of the darts of `p`.

This produces exactly the ordered list of oriented edges the walk crosses. The empty case is also right: a walk of length 0 has no darts. The definition makes sense for any simple graph on any vertex type, so it has the right generality. It is itself the Mathlib declaration for this notion, so no separate counterpart is listed.
